description: Substantial Roman settlement at a crossing of the River Tees. Earliest evidence of settlement is in the later 1st CE, and would begin to expand. In the 3rd CE a masonry structure was built which has been interpreted as a 'temple' due to a nearby dedication. It has also been suggested that the river crossing had previously been a religious focus due to a large number of finds in the river-bed. By the 4th CE occupation contracted into an associated fault, we can probably assume the temple is abandoned at this time, but occupation would last until the 7th - 8th CE.
